case_prompt: A 69-year-old female with an unremarkable past medical history presented for evaluation of persistent dyspepsia. She denied weight loss, anorexia, asthenia, or vomiting. Physical examination was normal. Upper endoscopy was performed and revealed a smooth bulge measuring 4 to 5 cm in diameter along the lesser curvature and the posterior wall of the stomach.
